update.title: Exposed Modular Flow Engine over HTTP with sink-defined results
update.summary: Exposed JSON flows through FastAPI and let sink destinations determine whether completed results return in the response, write to a file, or print to the console.

blocks.body:
## Call the same flows over HTTP

I exposed the engine’s JSON flows through a FastAPI service. Clients can list flows, inspect their inputs and components, validate a request, execute a flow, and check service health without importing engine internals. The CLI and HTTP service share one execution engine and one flow format.

blocks.label: Modular Flow Engine: JSON plans, components, and resume

blocks.code:
flowchart TD
  Request[HTTP execute request] --> Check{Return destination?}
  Check -->|Yes| Wait[Wait for result]
  Check -->|No| Accept[Accept background run]
  Wait --> Engine[Shared flow engine]
  Accept --> Engine
  Engine --> Sink{Declared sink destinations}
  Sink --> Return[API response]
  Sink --> File[JSON file]
  Sink --> Console[Console output]
blocks.description: The flow’s sink configuration determines both result delivery and the service’s default wait behavior.

blocks.body:
## Let sinks choose result delivery

A collector or JSON writer declares one or more destinations: `return`, `file`, or `console`. The service inspects those declarations before execution. A flow that returns data waits by default, while file- or console-only work can continue in the background; callers can override that choice explicitly.

blocks.description: One sink can return its completed value to the caller and write the same result to a file.
